html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. SDK: software development kit; MCP: Model Context Protocol

  • Programmatic enforcement (hooks, prerequisite gates) versus prompt-based guidance
  • When a rule needs deterministic compliance, and why prompts alone have a non-zero failure rate
  • Prerequisite gates that block a tool until an earlier step has finished
  • Structured handoffs when the agent escalates to a person
  • Hooks: PostToolUse to normalize results, and call interception to block policy violations

2Enforcement Versus Guidance

Running case

Birchwood Supply Stops Wrong Refunds

  • In 9% of conversations the support agent calls process_refund without first verifying the customer with get_customer
  • Some refunds went to the wrong account
  • The team has already written "ALWAYS verify the customer first" in the system prompt; the problem continues
Prompt-based guidance Programmatic enforcement
How it works Instructions, rules and examples in the prompt Code outside the model: hooks and prerequisite gates
Reliability Probabilistic: the model usually complies, but not always Deterministic: the code runs every time
Use when Style, preferences, soft ordering Identity checks before money moves, hard limits, legal or financial rules
  • When errors have financial or legal consequences, "usually" is not enough. A prompt has a non-zero failure rate; more emphasis or more examples reduce it but never remove it.

Exam tip

Requirement says "must", "always", "guarantee", money, identity or compliance? → programmatic enforcement. Answers that only strengthen the prompt, add few-shot examples or filter which tools exist are probabilistic or off-target.

3Prerequisite Gates and Multi-Concern Requests

  • Prerequisite gate: the code blocks a downstream tool call until the prerequisite step has completed. Example: process_refund and lookup_order stay blocked until get_customer has returned a verified customer ID.
  • The gate can live in the tool wrapper (check shared state) or in a hook (next section). The model sees a clear message such as "verify the customer first" and corrects itself.
  • Multi-concern requests ("my order is late and I was charged twice"): decompose the message into separate items, investigate each in parallel using shared context (for example the verified customer), then synthesize one unified resolution.

4Structured Handoffs to Humans

When the agent escalates, the human agent usually cannot see the conversation transcript. So the agent compiles a structured handoff summary:

Field Example
Customer ID C-48213 (verified)
Root cause Carrier damaged the parcel; photo evidence attached
Amount Refund of $189.00 requested
Actions taken Order located, return policy checked, refund blocked by the limit rule
Recommended action Approve a full refund and send a replacement
Exam tip

A handoff should be self-contained and structured, not "see transcript" and not a free-text paragraph.

5Hooks (Task 1.5)

Hooks are code that the SDK runs at fixed points of the agent loop, outside the model. Two patterns matter for the exam:

Hook pattern What it does Example
Tool-result hook (PostToolUse) Transforms the result before the model reads it Normalize Unix timestamps, ISO 8601 dates and numeric status codes from different MCP tools into one format
Tool-call interception (before the tool runs) Inspects the outgoing call and can block it or redirect it Block process_refund for amounts above $500 and send the case to human escalation
  • Deterministic guarantee (hook) versus probabilistic compliance (prompt): choose a hook when a business rule must hold every time.
async def cap_refunds(input_data, tool_use_id, context):
    if input_data["tool_name"] == "process_refund":
        if input_data["tool_input"].get("amount", 0) > 500:
            return {"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                "permissionDecision": "deny",
                "permissionDecisionReason": "Refunds over $500 need a human: use escalate_to_human."}}
    return {}

[Verify live] In current documentation, the call-interception hook is the PreToolUse event: it can deny a call (permissionDecision: "deny", or exit code 2 for shell hooks) with a reason that Claude sees, and can rewrite arguments with updatedInput. The result hook is PostToolUse: the tool has already run, so it cannot prevent the call, but it can replace the result with updatedToolOutput. Hooks are registered in the SDK hooks option (matcher such as "Bash" or "mcp__server__tool") or in settings files. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Choose the hook by what it acts on: the outgoing call (block or redirect) or the incoming result (normalize). A rule about money or identity is a call hook.

6Exam Q&A

S1Birchwood's agent sometimes calls process_refund before verifying the customer. The system prompt already says verification is mandatory. What change most effectively fixes this?

  • AAdd ten few-shot examples of correct verification
  • BAdd a programmatic prerequisite that blocks process_refund until get_customer returned a verified customer ID
  • CRepeat the verification instruction three times in the system prompt, in capital letters, at the start and end
  • DReduce the number of tools so the agent has fewer choices
Show the answer

Answer: B. A required order for a financial operation needs deterministic enforcement. Prompt wording and examples stay probabilistic, and fewer tools do not control order.

S2A mobile app sends refund amounts, and policy says refunds over $500 must be approved by a person. Which design guarantees the policy?

  • AA system prompt rule saying that the agent must never refund more than $500 under any circumstances
  • BA tool-call interception hook that blocks calls above $500 and redirects them to escalation
  • CA few-shot example showing an escalation for $600
  • DA note in CLAUDE.md
Show the answer

Answer: B. A hook enforces the threshold every time and can redirect to the right workflow. The others rely on the model following instructions.

S3Three MCP tools return dates as Unix timestamps, ISO 8601 strings and "MM/DD/YY" text, and the agent mixes up the order of events. What is the best approach?

  • ARemove the tools that return unusual date formats from the agent's tool list
  • BAsk the model in the prompt to convert all dates mentally before it compares them
  • CIncrease max_tokens
  • DUse a PostToolUse hook to normalize each result to one date format
Show the answer

Answer: D. A result-transforming hook gives the model consistent data deterministically, before it reads it.

S4When the agent escalates, support staff complain they cannot tell what was already done. The staff cannot open the chat transcript. What should the agent produce?

  • AA short message saying "customer is upset"
  • BA structured summary: customer ID, root cause, amount, actions taken, recommended action
  • CThe full raw conversation pasted into the ticket so that nothing is missing from the record
  • DNothing; staff should ask the customer again
Show the answer

Answer: B. Humans who cannot see the transcript need a structured, self-contained handoff to act on.

S5A customer writes: "My package is late and I see a duplicate charge." What is the best way to handle the two concerns?

  • AAnswer only the first issue and ignore the second
  • BDecompose into two items, investigate each in parallel with shared customer context, and give one unified resolution
  • CEscalate every multi-issue message to a human agent, because the agent cannot handle two concerns
  • DAsk the customer to send two separate messages
Show the answer

Answer: B. Decompose, investigate in parallel using shared context, then synthesize a single resolution.

S6Which statement about hooks versus prompts is correct?

  • AHooks give deterministic guarantees; prompts give probabilistic compliance
  • BHooks can only log events
  • CBoth give identical guarantees if the prompt is long enough
  • DHooks give probabilistic compliance and prompts give deterministic compliance
Show the answer

Answer: A. Hook code runs every time, so it gives deterministic guarantees; prompt instructions can be skipped with a small but non-zero probability.

S7Which requirement is the best candidate for a prompt instruction, not a hook?

  • AStop refunds that exceed a compliance limit
  • BNever delete production data
  • CPrefer a friendly tone when replying to customers
  • DBlock a wire transfer until multi-factor authentication succeeds
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tone is a soft preference where small variation is acceptable. The other three are hard rules that need enforcement.

S8Which TWO requirements should be enforced in code with a hook or gate rather than only in the prompt? Select TWO.

  • APrefer short answers
  • BBlock refunds above a fixed limit and send them to a person
  • CUse a warm, friendly tone
  • DVerify the customer's identity before any payment is made
  • EMention the help-center link when it fits
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Identity checks before money moves and hard monetary limits are non-negotiable rules that need deterministic enforcement. Tone, brevity and optional links are soft preferences.

S9Which TWO items belong in a structured handoff to a human agent? Select TWO.

  • ANothing, because humans can ask again
  • BThe customer's mood described in one word
  • CThe root cause found so far
  • DThe verified customer ID
  • EThe complete raw transcript pasted as one block
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. A handoff must be self-contained: identifiers and findings the human needs to act. A raw transcript or a mood word does not help, and asking the customer again wastes their time.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Enforce vs guide Hard rules (money, identity, compliance) → hooks or gates; soft style → prompt
Why prompts fall short Non-zero failure rate; more emphasis only lowers the odds
Prerequisite gate Block process_refund/lookup_order until get_customer returns a verified ID
Multi-concern request Decompose → investigate in parallel with shared context → one unified answer
Handoff Structured: customer ID, root cause, amount, actions taken, recommended action
PostToolUse hook Normalizes results (timestamps, ISO dates, status codes) before the model reads them
Interception hook Blocks/redirects calls (refund > $500 → human); event PreToolUse in current docs
